what_this_is: Phase 10's Exit measurement. Three arms on the documents this project actually ships, each run given its own fresh store, persisted as `weft eval run` records and held to this statement by `tests/docs/test_raptor_baseline.py`.
each_arm_replaces: the `extract` stage with `pdf-text` and the `embed` stage with `openai-embeddings`, and nothing else — so what is measured is the shipped rung, thresholds included, against a real embedder.
repetitions_are: Six for each raptor arm and three for the leaves arm. `L10.17` measured a three-repetition width as an estimate with more spread than the thing it estimates — two triples of one configuration spanned 0.0025 and 0.0215 — so three is not enough where a model writes the content. The leaves arm keeps three because it has scored identically to six decimal places every time it has been run, which is a claim about those runs and not proof it is deterministic.
each_run_has_its_own_store: `weft eval run` always indexes, so no two arms can be compared against one index (`L10.25`). Every run truncates first, asserts the store empty, and asserts it non-empty afterwards (`L8.30`).
minimum_detectable_effect_is: The wider of the two raptor arms' own six-repetition spreads, per metric. The leaves arm contributes nothing to it, having scored identically three times.
what_it_says: A null result, on every metric and every pair. The shipped one-level tree, the multi-level tree and leaves-only retrieval cannot be told apart on this corpus at this instrument's resolution — every difference is inside the minimum detectable effect, including multi-level against one-level, which is the direct test of whether deeper is better. The three differences against leaves-only are all slightly negative, so what evidence there is points away from the tree helping here rather than towards it; none of it clears the bar. Phase 10's Exit says a null result discharges it if it says so. It says so.
